Package neqsim.thermo.util.mineral

Class MineralMercuryBuffers

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.util.mineral.MineralMercuryBuffers
public final class MineralMercuryBuffers extends Object
Catalogue of mineral-fluid reactions that limit elemental mercury in petroleum reservoir fluids.

Elemental mercury in a reservoir fluid can be held back by two condensed phases: mercury sulfide (cinnabar, or the black polymorph metacinnabar) and liquid mercury. Each reaction is atom-balanced (checked on construction). The sulfide reactions use the CH4/CO2 pair of the reservoir fluid as redox agent, so the equilibrium mercury fugacity follows from the fluid without an assumed hydrogen fugacity. Mercury is the ideal-gas species named "mercury", which is also the NeqSim component name. Use SolidGasReactionEquilibrium.solveForGas(neqsim.thermo.system.SystemInterface, String) with target "mercury".

Reactions and the limiting mercury fugacity
Key Reaction f(Hg) proportional to
liquid-mercury Hg(l) = Hg(g) K (vapour pressure with the Poynting correction)
cinnabar-hydrogen HgS + H2 = Hg + H2S K f(H2)/f(H2S)
cinnabar-methane 4 HgS + CH4 + 2 H2O = 4 Hg + 4 H2S + CO2 (K f(CH4)/f(CO2))^(1/4) / f(H2S)
cinnabar-pyrite-siderite 8 HgS + 4 FeCO3 + CH4 = 8 Hg + 4 FeS2 + 5 CO2 + 2 H2O (K f(CH4)/f(CO2)^5)^(1/8)

The cinnabar-pyrite-siderite reaction is the cinnabar-methane reaction with the H2S fugacity fixed by the pyrite-siderite buffer of MineralH2SBuffers.pyriteSiderite(). The same four reactions are available for metacinnabar. The equilibria are upper limits: a fluid holds less mercury than the limit when the mercury supply from the source rock was smaller than the sulfide could hold back.
